outcomes.text: Explain the difference between a need and a want and how both change over time.
State that economic activity produces goods and services to satisfy needs and wants.
Identify the key decisions: what to produce, how to produce, and who benefits.
Describe consumers, producers and government as the main economic groups and how they interact.
Explain what an economic resource is.
Identify land, labour, capital and enterprise with examples and the reward each earns.
Explain the basic economic problem and how choices are made by weighing costs and benefits.
Explain opportunity cost in economic decisions.
Explain a market as buyers and sellers interacting to set a price.
Explain the role of markets in allocating scarce resources.
Distinguish factor markets from product markets.
Describe the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors and their relative sizes in the UK.
Distinguish a good from a service.
Explain specialisation and division of labour and why individuals and producers specialise.
Explain the costs and benefits of division of labour to the worker and the firm.
Explain what demand for a good or service means.
Identify the factors that influence demand.
Build an individual demand curve from consumer data.
Distinguish shifts of the demand curve from movements along it.
Explain what supply of a good or service means.
Identify the factors that influence supply.
Build a firm's supply curve from production data.
Distinguish shifts of the supply curve from movements along it.
Show how supply and demand set equilibrium price on a diagram.
Explain how excess demand and excess supply push prices to change.
Use diagrams to show the effect of changes on equilibrium price in real markets.
Show revenue on a supply and demand diagram.
Explain complements and substitutes.
Explain how a change in demand, supply or price in one market affects related markets.
Explain why price changes do not always cause equivalent changes in demand.
Name the factors affecting price elasticity of demand and distinguish elastic from inelastic demand.
Calculate price elasticity of demand as percentage change in quantity over percentage change in price.
Explain what elasticity of demand means for producers and consumers.
Explain why price changes do not always cause equivalent changes in supply.
Name the factors affecting price elasticity of supply and distinguish elastic from inelastic supply.
Calculate price elasticity of supply from data.
Explain what elasticity of supply means for producers and consumers.
Describe business objectives: profit, sales growth and market share.
Identify and calculate total, average, fixed and variable costs.
Identify and calculate total and average revenue.
Show that profit is total revenue minus total costs and how firms raise it by cutting average costs or raising revenue.
Explain how higher prices and profits give producers the incentive to expand.
Explain how producers' motives can conflict with ethical and moral interests.
Distinguish production from productivity.
Name the factors that influence productivity and the benefits of raising it.
Define economies of scale as the effect on average cost of rising output.
Describe managerial, purchasing, financial, technical and risk-bearing economies of scale.
Explain the effects of economies of scale on business behaviour and the costs and benefits of growth.
Explain diseconomies of scale.
Explain that markets differ in structure.
Use number of producers, product differentiation and ease of entry to tell market structures apart.
Describe the main characteristics of a competitive market and how producers operate in it.
Explain the effect of competition on consumers, producers and workers, and why profits tend to be lower.
Describe the characteristics of a non-competitive market and how producers operate in it.
Define monopoly and oligopoly.
Explain the causes and consequences of monopolistic and oligopolistic power.
Explain how wages are set by simple labour demand and supply.
Explain wage differences within and between occupations.
Distinguish gross from net pay and calculate income.
Define market failure as the market's inability to allocate resources efficiently.
Explain the costs of misallocating resources.
Describe government methods to counter misallocation.
Define externalities as the gap between social and private costs or benefits.
Identify positive and negative externalities.
Explain how production and consumption can create negative externalities.
Explain what an interest rate is and what influences different rates.
Explain how interest rate changes affect consumers' decisions to save, borrow or spend.
Explain how interest rate changes affect producers' decisions to save, borrow or invest.
Calculate interest on savings.
Identify the main sources of UK government revenue and areas of spending.
Distinguish direct from indirect taxes.
Distinguish progressive from regressive taxes.
State the principal objectives: full employment, price stability, economic growth and balance of payments.
Explain how a policy for one objective can harm another.
Describe other objectives such as reducing inequality and managing environmental change.
Explain how pursuing an objective can harm groups of people.
Explain what economic growth means and why it matters.
Distinguish GDP, real GDP and GDP per capita and do simple calculations.
Describe the causes, costs, benefits and policies for growth.
Describe how employment and unemployment are measured.
Explain structural, seasonal, frictional and cyclical unemployment and their causes.
Explain the consequences of unemployment and policies to reduce it.
Explain inflation and its rate, and measure it with the Consumer Price Index.
Do simple calculations with CPI figures.
Explain cost-push and demand-pull inflation.
Explain consequences of inflation for different groups and policies to manage it.
Do simple calculations using current account figures.
Explain what a current account deficit or surplus means and why it matters.
Explain the reasons for a deficit or surplus and policies to influence it.
Describe the distribution of income in the UK.
Explain the causes and consequences of income and wealth inequality.
Explain how taxation and government spending redistribute income and wealth.

topics.title: 3.2.3 How the government manages the economy

outcomes.text: Explain how fiscal policy changes income and spending in the economy.
Explain how fiscal policy helps achieve government objectives.
Explain a balanced budget and the consequences of a budget surplus or deficit.
Explain what monetary policy is.
Explain how monetary policy controls inflation and serves other objectives.
Evaluate supply-side policies: education and training, lower taxes, trade union reform and privatisation or deregulation.
Explain how supply-side policies help achieve government objectives.
Describe government policies to influence positive and negative externalities.

topics.title: 3.2.4 International trade and the global economy

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of trade to economies and to the UK.
Describe the UK's main exports and imports.
Explain the advantages of trade and the consequences of global interdependence.
Explain how demand and supply determine exchange rates.
Explain how exchange rate changes affect consumers and producers.
Give arguments for and against free trade.
Explain the significance and benefits of free-trade agreements such as the EU.
Describe the factors behind globalisation, including technology and multinational companies.
Explain the benefits and drawbacks of globalisation for producers, workers and consumers in the UK and less developed countries.
Explain moral, ethical and sustainability issues in international trade.

topics.title: 3.2.5 The role of money and financial markets

outcomes.text: Describe money's functions: deferred payment, store of value, unit of account and medium of exchange.
Explain that money is more than notes and coins in circulation.
Identify the Bank of England, commercial banks and building societies.
Explain the Bank of England's role in influencing interest rates and keeping the system stable.
Explain how high street banks fund investment and serve savers and borrowers.
